title: Magnetic Materials
seo_title: Year 3 Science: Magnetic Materials Worksheets (Iron, Steel and Not All Metals)
standard_text: Compare and group together a variety of everyday materials on the basis of whether they are attracted to a magnet, and identify some magnetic materials.
meta_desc: Free Year 3 science worksheets on magnetic materials: which materials magnets attract, iron and steel, metals that are not magnetic, testing and sorting with magnets. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: Not all metals are magnetic: aluminium and copper are not.
body_html:
How to think about it

Only some materials are attracted to magnets.

  • Magnetic materials: iron, steel, nickel and cobalt.
  • Not all metals are magnetic: aluminium, copper, brass, gold and silver are not. Plastic, wood, glass and fabric are not.
  • Magnets can sort materials, such as steel cans from aluminium cans.
Example

Steel paperclip: magnetic?

Steel contains iron

Answer: Yes

Example

Aluminium can: magnetic?

A metal, but not magnetic

Answer: No

Common mistakes

  • Thinking all metals are magnetic.
  • Thinking shiny things are magnetic.
  • Thinking magnets attract aluminium foil.

faq.a: Iron, steel (which is mostly iron), nickel and cobalt. Things made from them, like steel paperclips and iron nails, are attracted to magnets.
No. Aluminium, copper, brass, gold and silver are metals that are not attracted to magnets.

faq.q: How are magnets used to sort materials?
faq.a: Recycling centres use magnets to pull steel cans out from aluminium cans. You can also use a magnet to separate iron filings from sand.
